DIA_G02: Menstruation is over and estrogen is rising. Welcome to the follicular phase: your energy, mood and confidence are all coming back.
DIA_G03: This time we climb. Up in the ovary a tiny egg is maturing inside a follicle, and the higher we get, the brighter it gets.
DIA_G04: The iron you collected in the cave is your fuel now. Keep gathering it, use <KB>arrows</KB><GP>D-pad</GP> to move and <KB>UP / Space</KB><GP>🟡</GP> to jump. Let's go!
DIA_G05: These bubbles are follicles. Every cycle a few of them grow, but only one wins. The pink ones hold you; the yellow ones burst after a moment, so keep moving.
DIA_G06: Feel that warm air? Estrogen lifts you up. Step into the stream and it carries you higher than any jump.
DIA_G07: Careful: distractions. Notifications, tiredness, temptations... they don't hurt, but they slow you down. Dodge them, or blow them away with your breath (<KB>CTRL</KB><GP>🔴</GP>).
DIA_G08: Almost at the top. When estrogen peaks, the brain sends out a big wave of LH, the hormone that releases the egg. When it comes, don't stop climbing.
DIA_G10: Time for a snack. Your body wants to turn the iron from the cave into fresh red blood cells, but iron is picky about company.

DIA_G12: Perfect plate! Lentils and seeds bring the iron; the orange and the pepper bring vitamin C, which helps your gut take it in.
DIA_G13: Tea and coffee are fine, just not right with an iron-rich meal. Wait an hour or two. And your legs feel springier already: you jump higher now!
DIA_G14: Full of energy? That's estrogen. In the follicular phase your body recovers faster and loves to move: running, dancing, a hard workout.
DIA_G15: Catch the rhythm: press when a beat lands in the ring. Ten good hits and you've got it.
DIA_G16: That's the rhythm! Moving in this phase makes you stronger and lifts your mood, and it even eases the cramps in the next cycle.
DIA_G17: Here's your reward: press <KB>Shift</KB><GP>🟢</GP> to dash. A short burst forward, and distractions bounce right off you.
DIA_G18: Your body talks all month long. If you learn its language, nothing in the cycle surprises you anymore.
DIA_G19: Sort the signals into the four phases: menstruation, follicular, ovulation and luteal. Like a cycle-tracking app, but you are the app.
DIA_G20: Exactly. A cycle usually takes 21 to 35 days, and in the first years it can be irregular; that's normal. Writing it down helps you see what's yours.
DIA_G21: Signals that are not normal: bleeding through a pad every hour, pain that stops you from living, or periods that vanish for months. Then you talk to a doctor.
DIA_G22: And your body is at full power now: your double jump goes higher. Up we go!
DIA_G23: Here it comes! Estrogen peaked and the brain released the LH wave, the signal for ovulation. It rises fast.
DIA_G24: Climb! Reach the summit before the wave reaches you. Use everything you've got: jump, dash, the updrafts!
DIA_G25: You made it! The egg is released: this is ovulation, the peak of the cycle. It lives for about a day, waiting in the fallopian tube.
DIA_G26: Around now you feel your best: confident, social, full of energy. These few days are also the fertile window, the days when a pregnancy can begin.
DIA_G27: Knowing where you are in your cycle means no surprises. Well done, keeper. The next phase is coming, but that's a story for another day.

FOOD_LENTILS_FACT: Full of iron, like beans and chickpeas.
FOOD_SEEDS_FACT: A handful covers a good part of your daily iron.
FOOD_ORANGE_FACT: Vitamin C can double how much iron you absorb.
FOOD_PEPPER_FACT: More vitamin C than an orange. Iron's best friend.
FOOD_TEA_FACT: Tannins in tea bind iron, so it passes right through.
FOOD_COFFEE_FACT: Coffee with a meal can cut iron absorption by more than a third.
FOOD_COLA_FACT: Caffeine and sugar, nothing for your blood. Water instead!
FOOD_CANDY_FACT: A sugar rush, then a crash. No iron in there.

DIA_M01: Hm? I'm... outside. Everything is green and wet, like after rain.
DIA_M02: Hi hi hi! Finally awake! I'm Iskra. I wake things up: you, the garden, the little seeds. Come on, come on, this way!
DIA_M03: Easy, Iskra. Kyra, this is the follicular phase: your body is rebuilding and estrogen is rising. The river below is the last cycle flowing away: old water, cold and slow to wade through. Stay up on the leaves where you can.
DIA_M04: The vessel wants new water: the dew the morning left on the leaves up there. The fuller it is, the more your thread can do. And the light seeds? You don't grab those. Aim at one and hold <KB>the mouse button or E</KB><GP>LB</GP>: the thread pulls it in.
DIA_M05: A seed! See it glow? Aim at it, hold, and don't let go until it's in your hand. Let go too early and it slips away. Ten of them, plus a full vessel, and the gate opens.
DIA_M06: That river is what's flowing away: the last cycle, used up. You can wade through it, but it's slow and it pushes you back, so climb out where you can. It won't fill the vessel; only the dew up on the leaves does.
DIA_M07: When you focus, shadows may come: stress, worries, noise. They only hurt while you hold the thread. Let go, or jump, and they pass. If one hits you, you lose water and the gate moves further away. Stress really does delay ovulation.
DIA_M08: The gate is close! It opens when the vessel is full and you've got ten seeds. Missing some? Go back for them, the meadow isn't going anywhere.
DIA_M09: Not yet! The gate wants a full vessel and ten seeds. Look around, there's more to find.
DIA_M10: Let's use this clear head. In the follicular phase many people find it easier to focus.
DIA_M11: Look at the scene for a moment and remember as many things as you can. Then pick the ones you saw. No losing here: every one you find counts.
DIA_M12: Nice. Estrogen can help memory and focus a little, but research shows small differences, and everyone is different.
DIA_M13: Every phase of the cycle has its strength. This one is good for starting new things.
DIA_M14: Your body is building a new lining inside the womb: a soft, well-fed bed. It needs good food.
DIA_M15: Catch the beans, nuts, vegetables, fish and fruit on the cushion. Dodge the lightning: that's stress, and it thins the cushion.
DIA_M16: The cushion is thick and full. That's the endometrium: a safe, nourishing layer the body builds every cycle.
DIA_M17: Big stress disturbs this. The body reads it as danger and can delay ovulation. So eat well, and take breaks.
DIA_M18: Your body sends signals all through this phase. Pair each one with what it means.
DIA_M19: You read your body well. Not every pair had to be right on the first try; the point is to slow down and notice.
DIA_M20: One more thing: a sharp twinge low in the belly around the middle of the cycle can be ovulation itself. Nothing to worry about.
DIA_M21: The vessel is full... and the seeds are warm in my hand.
DIA_M23: Look! A golden flower! That's the one follicle that won; the egg inside is ready. Up, up, up we go next!
